chapter.heading: Damascus: A Pile of Dust and Rubble
chapter.v:
A message
about Damascus. Look, Damascus will cease to exist as a city. Instead it will become a pile of ruins.

The towns
of Aroer will be abandoned. Flocks will live in the streets and rest there, because there won't be anyone to chase them away.

The fortified
city will disappear from Ephraim, Damascus will no longer be a kingdom, and those that are left of the Arameans will be like the lost glory of Israel, declares the Lord Almighty.
chapter.heading: The Day Is Coming
chapter.v:
At that
time the glory of Jacob will fade away; he will lose his strength.

It will
look as empty as fields after reapers have harvested the grain, gathering up the grain in their arms. It will be like when people pick the heads of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.

Yet there
will be some left behind, like an olive tree that has been shaken—two or three ripe olives are left at the top of the tree, four or five on its lower branches, declares the Lord, the God of Israel.

At that
time people will pay attention to their Creator and look to the Holy One of Israel.

They won't
believe in the altars they built and the idols they made; they will not look to the Asherah poles or the altars of incense.

At that
time their fortified cities will be like places left to be taken over by bushes and trees, just as they were previously abandoned when the Israelites invaded. The country will become completely desolate.
chapter.heading: You Have Forgotten God
chapter.v:
You have
forgotten the God who saves you; you have not remembered the Rock who protects you. So, even though you plant beautiful plants and grow exotic vines,

even though
you make them grow on the day that you plant them, and have them blossom in the morning that you sow them, your harvest will be a heap of trouble on a day of grief and pain that cannot be cured.

Disaster is
coming to the many nations that growl, growling like the raging sea! Disaster is coming to the peoples who roar, roaring like thundering waters!

The nations
roar like the roaring of crashing waves. But he confronts them, and they run far away, blown by the wind like chaff on the mountains, like tumbleweeds driven by a storm.

Sudden terror
comes in the evening! By morning, they're gone! This is what happens to those who loot us, the fate of those who plunder us.
